QUESTION ONE: Prose

Refer to Text A, "Eugene", on page 2 of the resource booklet.

Analyse how the writer uses language to show the relationship between Eugene and his mother.

Support your answer with evidence from the text.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement (3-4): Engage with the text by addressing the question, exploring a relevant idea using analysis-related terminology. Show awareness that meaning has been deliberately crafted. Include specific and relevant details from the text. Merit (5-6): Convincingly address the question, presenting a reasoned and clear discussion of one or more ideas using analysis-related terminology. Show awareness that meaning has been deliberately crafted for a particular purpose. Weave a range of specific details from the text to support the main idea(s). Excellence (7-8): Develop an insightful or original argument or interpretation of the text. Make judgments about how effects and meanings relate to the purpose of the text. Weave a range of specific and relevant details to support the argument or interpretation. Ideas might include: Eugene is lively, sometimes exasperatingly so (sprawling, burning, whooped, hollered, clattered); the calmness of the mother is contrasted with the unpredictability of the child, she reacts with affection and sympathy; the originality of language (e.g. 'roister-doister', 'ratbag') depicts Eugene as a unique child and emphasises how young he is.

QUESTION TWO: Poetry

Refer to Text B, "Timepiece", on page 3 of the resource booklet.

Analyse how the poet expresses their attitude towards the time spent doing chores.

Support your answer with evidence from the text.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement (3-4): Engage with the text by addressing the question, exploring a relevant idea using analysis-related terminology. Show awareness that meaning has been deliberately crafted. Include specific details from the text. Merit (5-6): Convincingly address the question, presenting a reasoned discussion of one or more ideas. Show awareness of deliberate crafting for a particular purpose. Weave a range of specific details. Excellence (7-8): Develop an insightful or original argument or interpretation. Make judgments about how effects and meanings relate to the purpose of the text. Ideas might include: how time can seem to stand still when doing chores; how there can be a sense of satisfaction or reward in completing chores; how you can find freedom once the chores have been finished.

Analyse how the writer conveys the experience of dealing with milk skin.

Support your answer with evidence from the text.

Show awareness that meaning has been deliberately crafted. Include specific details from the text. Merit (5-6): Convincingly address the question, presenting a reasoned discussion of one or more ideas. Show awareness of deliberate crafting for a particular purpose.
